note: Built as ballot/lean/mn_endorsements.json is. Each record is one line of one party page, matched to one race and one candidate on the official lists already loaded in ballot_local_2026.sqlite (office, place and name all fit, one fit only). Missouri differs from Minnesota: its parties nominate in the August 4 partisan primary, county offices and circuit judges included, and afterwards their pages list their nominees; very few party pages endorse anyone. Only a page that itself says 'endorse' or 'endorsed' for a named candidate in a 2026 race, on a party committee's own site, is under endorsements: two county committees' pages (Cass County's, published before the primary, and Boone County's). Under other_support, kept apart and not for showing as an endorsement, with the page's own word in 'kind': the Jackson County Republican Committee's 'GOP Voter Guide' (a list of the party's November nominees that does not say endorsed), and the August primary endorsements of the South Kansas City Democrats, which is a Democratic club and not a committee of the party. A bare list of a party's nominees is not collected: it adds nothing to the party label already on the ballot. The state parties endorsed positions on ballot questions only; ballot questions, federal offices and party offices are outside this file. 'election' appears only when the candidate is on a primary list and not on the November list. Names are spelled as our record spells them; 'as_listed' keeps the page's wording. Read on 2026-10-02 with the kit's honest User-Agent, each site's robots.txt checked first: the four state parties' sites (Democratic, Republican, Libertarian, Green), and every county unit's own website linked from the Democratic and Republican state directories or found by search (home page plus its candidate, election and news pages, ten pages a site at most; every page was searched for the words endorse, recommend, slate and voter guide, not read line by line). Most county units have only a social media page, which is never read. Every page in 'lists' was opened again after it was read, and a record is kept only if the page still showed it. No site read forbids programs in its robots.txt, so nothing is held. 'not_read' names the pages looked at and why nothing was taken, and the units that could not or should not be read.
